security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel (running in S-mode) writes to sstatus.SUM, sstatus.MXR, or the M-mode firmware writes to mstatus.TVM/TSR/TW/MPRV expecting the bit to take effect, but the RISC-V implementation incorrectly makes the bit read-only 0 despite the spec-required condition for writability being met (e.g., S-mode supported with satp.MODE writable for SUM/MXR/TVM, U-mode supported for MPRV, modes less privileged than M exist for TW)
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: csrw sstatus.*SSTATUS_SUM|csrs sstatus.*SSTATUS_MXR|writing mstatus CSR with TVM|TSR|TW|MPRV bits set without checking WARL readback
security_spec.summary: Spec now requires mstatus control bits (SUM, MXR, TVM, TSR, TW, MPRV, MIE/MPIE) to be writable when the corresponding feature is supported — a non-conformant implementation that makes these bits read-only 0 despite supporting the feature would silently break FreeBSD's memory protection model and trap virtualization controls

findings.finding: ENTER_USER_ACCESS/EXIT_USER_ACCESS macros use csrs/csrc on sstatus.SUM without WARL readback verification. If a RISC-V implementation incorrectly makes SUM read-only 0 (despite the spec-required condition of S-mode with writable satp.MODE being met), all copyin/copyout/fueword/suword operations would fail, resulting in function_loss. The kernel blindly trusts the CSR write succeeded with no readback check.
findings.snippet:
#define	ENTER_USER_ACCESS(tmp)						\
	li	tmp, SSTATUS_SUM;					\
	csrs	sstatus, tmp

#define	EXIT_USER_ACCESS(tmp)						\
	li	tmp, SSTATUS_SUM;					\
	csrc	sstatus, tmp

findings.finding: On S-mode exception entry, SUM is explicitly cleared via csrc sstatus,SSTATUS_SUM before the saved sstatus is stored to the trapframe. This is correct defensive practice ensuring SUM is never left set across exception handlers. The KASSERTs in trap.c:315 and trap.c:396 further verify SUM is always 0 on trap entry for both S-mode and U-mode exceptions.
findings.snippet:
.if \mode == 1
	/* Disable user address access for supervisor mode exceptions. */
	li	t0, SSTATUS_SUM
	csrc	sstatus, t0
.endif

findings.finding: fork_trampoline restores sstatus from the trapframe via csrw sstatus,t0. The restored value comes from TF_SSTATUS which was saved during save_registers, where SUM was already cleared for S-mode entries. For newly forked user processes, the sstatus in the frame should also have SUM=0 initialized. No risk of restoring SUM=1 inadvertently.

vmmops_vcpu_init sets HSTATUS_VTW in the guest hstatus for hypervisor context. This is correct hypervisor behavior: VTW controls whether WFI from VS-mode traps to HS-mode. This is not a write to mstatus.TW - the hypervisor uses hstatus CSR (HS-level) to virtualize the TW constraint for guests. The kernel never writes mstatus.TW directly.

The kernel defines MSTATUS_MPRV (bit 17) but never writes mstatus CSR from S-mode (confirmed: zero csrw/csrs/csrc on mstatus). MPRV and TVM/TSR/TW are M-mode-only fields; FreeBSD kernel runs in S-mode and cannot directly modify them. M-mode firmware (OpenSBI) is responsible for mstatus.TW, and the kernel interacts with firmware via SBI calls that do not expose mstatus manipulation.

No SSTATUS_MXR definition exists anywhere in the RISC-V port. The kernel does not use MXR (bit 19 of sstatus) for execute-only page support. The absense of MXR usage means there is no risk of the kernel relying on an incorrectly-WARL'd MXR bit. This is a known limitation (the kernel lacks execute-only support) but not a security violation per this spec.
findings.snippet:
#define	SSTATUS_UIE			(1 << 0)
#define	SSTATUS_SIE			(1 << 1)
...
#define	SSTATUS_SUM			(1 << 18)
/* No SSTATUS_MXR defined */
